supersedes: submissions/secp256k1-ecdlp/automorphism-rho-v2 (rejected: period-3 fruitless cycles from the order-3 identity, ledger sum 644 vs stated 641, memory strictly > 2^70, lag-as-mean)
heuristics: H1: the canonical 32-adding walk on the (r-1)/6 automorphism classes has first-collision time approximating the birthday tail 1 - exp(-t^2/(2N)); supported classically, by Teske's r-adding-walk experiments, and by the toy run (0.545 vs 0.4845 ideal in the lag-free regime).

Fruitless-cycle handling: the period-2 negation family (rate ~1/192, census-measured 1/115, charged bound 1/64) and the period-3 order-identity family (rate ~2^-16.7, proven algebraically via 1+lam+lam^2=0) are detected by dual look-backs at distances 2 and 3 with full-state fruitless/useful discrimination and one-addition escapes, all charged. Longer zero-sum families of the multiplier ring are bounded by pattern counting (< 2^-40 per step) and fenced by a per-walker epoch limit of 2^36 steps, under which any family entering below 2^-31.4 per step wastes at most the charged 5% residual slack.
limitations: Analytic construction; no production-size execution is claimed or possible.
Single-shot randomized attack with success probability lower bound 0.39 exactly at the protected threshold; no amplification is used and all failures are charged.

The distinguished-point table is a hard 2^63-slot allocation; the peak is strictly above 2^70 bytes and reported as 70.1; overflow aborts with probability <= exp(-2^58.2) (Chernoff, correct ratio 0.065).
Automorphism-accelerated rho is standard cryptanalysis, not a novel attack; this is the first qualified bound for this track under the protected cost model.
